To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of a multi-resolution dataset on disk-based storage cluster is significantly affected by: 1) the data declustering strategy; 2) the index size; 3) the query processing strategy; and 4) the number of clients.

(a) a data declustering strategy that uses a combination of data replication and data partitioning is superior to a data partitioning only strategy, and (b) an index structure that uses a combination a spatial and a temporal index is superior to a spatial index only structure.

(i) the performance of the query processing algorithms depends on how the datasets are declustered on the storage cluster, (ii) the performance depends on how the data is indexed on the storage cluster and (iii) the performance of data processing operations (sampling and aggregation) depends on how the query is processed and how the data is declustered and indexed on the storage and compute clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the development and implementation of a data server that supports the storage, indexing, retrieval, and visualization of multi-resolution Grid datasets; (2) the development of a suite of data processing algorithms for the computation of aggregate queries over multi-resolution Grid datasets, (3) the development of an efficient data declustering algorithm for multi-resolution Grid datasets on storage clusters, (4) the development of efficient query processing strategies that use data declustering and indexing to support the efficient execution of aggregate

the following issues: (1) how to store and index multi-resolution datasets on distributed disk clusters; (2) how to efficiently query the data on such clusters; and (3) how to support data sampling and data aggregation on such clusters.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach to data declustering, data sampling and query processing is very effective for large multi-resolution datasets and that the proposed approach is a promising approach to support the efficient querying of very high-resolution datasets on storage clusters.
the performance of the data server is strongly dependent on the query type, the query parameters, and the data distribution.
our data server is a viable alternative for the storage and retrieval of multi-resolution volumetric data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of multi-resolution data declustering and multi-resolution index structures can significantly improve the performance of data processing services and queries.
the use of multi-resolution data structures for large datasets is beneficial, but only when the data is stored and queried in a distributed manner, i.e., using storage and compute clusters.

we can serve large multi-resolution datasets efficiently using a disk-based storage cluster and that we can achieve significant performance improvements over the state-of-the-art by using a data declustering and indexing strategy that is based on the multi-resolution nature of the datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data declustering is a key factor in the performance of data servers for multi-resolution data.
the choice of the declustering strategy and the indexing scheme has a significant impact on query performance.
the choice of data declustering, index, and query processing strategy has significant impact on the query performance.
